summary: Configured snapshot-backed XFS storage at /srv/data on node1. Modified the data, restored the earlier snapshot exactly, and verified persistence after a full node reboot without changing RHEL 7.9 or kernel 3.10.0-1160.
actions_performed: Created a dedicated 2 GiB XFS filesystem using legacy-compatible device-mapper snapshots.
Installed the srvdata-snapshot utility with create, restore, setup, and status operations.
Enabled srvdata.service to reconstruct and mount the filesystem during boot.
Captured baseline data, created a read-only snapshot, modified/deleted files, and restored via block-level snapshot merge.
Verified identical file hashes, metadata, directory structure, and symlink target after restoration.
Rebooted node1 and confirmed its boot identity changed and all storage/data recovered.

evidence.summary: /srv/data is a dedicated XFS device-mapper filesystem; its service is enabled, and a persistent read-only snapshot exposed the captured data and hashes.

evidence.requirement: Restore the exact content captured before modification
evidence.summary: The live data diverged after modification while the snapshot stayed unchanged. Snapshot merge restored the original manifest and SHA-256 hashes exactly, recovered deleted objects, and removed post-snapshot data.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Before and after implementation/reboot, the node remained RHEL Server 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64.
Captured healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, acknowledged the safe reboot, observed a changed boot ID, then proved the service, XFS mount, device mapping, and exact restored data recovered.
